issues.failure_explanation: An arbitrary generalized Schur decomposition does not put one copy of each distinct mu_i in its leading ell-dimensional deflating subspace. For B0=B2=I2 and B1=diag(-2,2), the unique desired solvent is diag(1,-1), but a valid Schur ordering can place both copies of eigenvalue 1 first. That leading subspace is the complete Jordan subspace for the first coordinate, so Z11 has rank one and the prescribed inverse does not exist. Modulus ordering cannot resolve this because all eigenvalues have modulus one.
